scenes.location: Apartment balcony and the street below
scenes.light: Warm window light behind Mia; cool blue street; one streetlight on the corner

beats.action: From the street: a lit third-floor window, and in front of it a small figure on tiptoe at the balcony rail, chin just over the top. Below her, an empty parking bay at the kerb. The streetlight on the corner flickers on.
beats.effect: A quiet evening; this small person is waiting for something.

delivery.intent: Matter-of-fact scene-setting, with quiet fondness for a nightly ritual
delivery.inflection: Falling on both sentences; 'watch' settles but doesn't sound final
breaths: After 'watch', in the gap before shot 2
delivery.note: Starts just after the streetlight ticks on

beats.action: Close, through the balusters: Mia leans to one side, peering down the street towards the corner, holding the rail with both hands.
beats.effect: We know what she wants and feel her patience.

spoken.speaker: narrator
spoken.text: She knows the sound of Dad's car.

delivery.marked: (breath) She knows the sound of Dad's car.
delivery.intent: Shares a family fact, slightly confiding: everyone in this flat knows it
delivery.inflection: A small lift on 'knows'; land 'car' cleanly and falling. Don't lean on 'Dad's'
delivery.pace: Even; no pause inside the line, because 'car' is a cue word
breaths: Then a long silent breath through beat b3
delivery.note: The cut into this shot lands 10 frames before 'car'
delivery.placedBy: sh2's anchor: the cut lands 10 frames before 'car'

beats.action: Looking down from the balcony: an engine grows from somewhere out of sight, then a single bright light swings round the corner under the streetlight. Mia, at the edge of frame, rises higher on her toes.
beats.effect: Hope: this is it. A held silent beat before the twist.
beats.readingNote: No words. The engine carries this beat; the reader breathes here, silently.

beats.action: The light belongs to a delivery scooter, a pizza box strapped on the back, pulling up to her building.
beats.effect: Surprise and a small letdown: not Dad.

delivery.intent: Deadpan correction, almost a shrug, but every word clear: this line is the turn of the film
delivery.inflection: Flat on 'Not', then a small, definite fall on 'Dad'
delivery.pace: Unhurried for its two words: a hair of air between 'Not' and 'Dad', and a clearly voiced D on 'Dad'. Deadpan is flat, not rushed
breaths: Before 'Not', silent (taken in the b3 silence)
After 'Dad', silent, through the rest of the shot
delivery.note: Comes just after the scooter's brake squeak, not on the cut
delivery.placedBy: sh4's anchor: 'Not' lands 8 frames after the cut, just after the brake squeak
delivery.revised: 2026-11-24: take 1, read 'quick and short', was too clipped to make out on a speaker (the human, and the transcriber, heard 'Not that')

beats.action: Mia throws both arms high above the rail, up on her toes, the warm window glowing behind her.
beats.effect: Delight; the joke lands on her reaction.

delivery.intent: The one warm moment: the smile is finally audible, still understated
delivery.inflection: A gentle lift on 'Even', settling down on 'better'; ends falling and soft
breaths: A small audible intake before 'Even', like the start of a smile
None after; silence and music to the end
delivery.note: After her arms go up; then nothing more is said
delivery.placedBy: sh5's anchor: 'better' lands 36 frames after the cut, so 'Even' starts about 0.9 s in

voiceDirection.who: A dry, deadpan Australian man, 40s to 50s, telling a story he knows well and is quietly fond of
voiceDirection.register: Understated. The humour is in restraint: never sell a line
voiceDirection.pace: Unhurried, about 2 words per second; let the pictures breathe
voiceDirection.mic: Close and intimate, as if sitting beside the listener
avoid: rising inflection at the end of statements
audible smiling before the last line
voiceDirection.marks: In 'marked': (breath) = a breath point; | = a pause without a breath; timings in seconds from the start of the shot
